Title: Accurate binaural mirroring of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions suggests influence of time-locking in medial efferents.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs)
Evidence_Quote: Spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs) of nearly identical acoustic frequency in both ears are a common observation

Title: A developmental study of distortion product otoacoustic emission (2f1-f2) suppression in humans.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 14 normal-hearing adults, 33 term and 85 premature neonates
Outcome: premature neonates show narrower STCs and atypical suppression growth at f2 of 1500 and 6000 Hz, indicating immature cochlear frequency resolution
Evidence_Quote: Premature neonates showed non-adult-like DPOAE suppression at f2 of 1500 and 6000 Hz

Title: State transitions in uncomplicated pregnancies after term.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: low risk term fetuses (39-41 weeks post menstrual age)
Outcome: behavioural state transitions; fetal heart rate pattern; eye and body movements
Evidence_Quote: We investigated whether state transitions in twelve low risk term fetuses (39-41 weeks post menstrual age, PMA; control group) differ from those in twelve uncomplicated pregnancies > 41 weeks PMA (study group).

Title: Role of experience for language-specific functional mappings of vowel sounds.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: response to vowel tokens; generalization
Evidence_Quote: eight European starlings (Sturnus vulgaris) were trained to respond differentially to vowel tokens drawn from stylized distributions for the English vowels /i/ and /I/, or from two distributions of vowel sounds that were orthogonal in the F1-F2 plane.

Title: Gender distinctions and lateral asymmetry in the low-level auditory brainstem response of the human neonate.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: male infants have lower ABR thresholds than females (right-ear difference 7.45 dB, left-ear 1.56 dB); right-ear advantage in wave V amplitude
Evidence_Quote: Threshold measures of auditory brainstem response (ABR) were generated in 72 full-term newborn infants in response to clicks and tone burst stimuli between 500 and 8000 Hz as detailed in a previous study.

Title: The effect of the evanescent wave upon acoustic measurements in the human ear canal.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: no participants (theoretical predictions for human adults and 1-month-old infants)
Stimulus_Type: none (theoretical model of ear-canal acoustic measurement)
Outcome: evanescent-wave error below 10 kHz predicted at 3 dB in adults and 1.3 dB in 1-month-old infants
Evidence_Quote: The maximum measurement error due to the presence of the evanescent wave in human ear canals below 10 kHz is predicted to be 3 dB in adults and 1.3 dB in 1 month old infants, when the loudspeaker and microphone ports are spaced more than 2 mm apart.

Title: Effect of stimulus level and frequency on ABR and MLR binaural interaction in human neonates.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: auditory brainstem response; middle latency response; binaural interaction
Evidence_Quote: Auditory brainstem (ABR) and middle latency (MLR) responses were evoked by click and tone-burst stimuli from human neonates.

Title: Auditory threshold sensitivity of the human neonate as measured by the auditory brainstem response.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: healthy, full-term human neonates and young adults
Stimulus_Type: clicks and tone-bursts of 0.5, 1.5, 4.0 and 8.0 kHz embedded in notched noise (ABR)
Outcome: infant ABR thresholds elevated by 3-25 dB relative to adult thresholds, greatest for high-frequency stimuli
Evidence_Quote: ABRs were elicited with clicks and tone-bursts of 0.5, 1.5, 4.0 and 8.0 kHz, embedded in notched noise, in healthy, full-term human neonates

Title: Anatomy of the normal human cochlear aqueduct with functional implications.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 101 human temporal bones, ages 0-100 years (19 aged 0-1 years)
Stimulus_Type: none (temporal-bone anatomy; quantitative model of aqueduct function)
Outcome: aqueduct patency types and dimensions described; model suggests little effect on sound transmission above 20 Hz in normal ears
Evidence_Quote: has little effect on normal ossicular transmission of sound for frequencies above 20 Hz. In pathological ears, such as those with ossicular disruption or after a type IV tympanoplasty, a patent aqueduct might affect hearing for frequencies below 150 Hz.

Title: The acoustic features of vowel-like grunt calls in chacma baboons (Papio cyncephalus ursinus): implications for production processes and functions.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: acoustic features of grunt calls
Evidence_Quote: The acoustic features of 216 baboon grunts were investigated through analysis of field-recorded calls produced by identified females in known contexts.

Title: Rate and adaptation effects on the auditory evoked brainstem response in human newborns and adults.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: auditory evoked brainstem response latencies; auditory evoked brainstem response amplitudes
Evidence_Quote: Auditory evoked brainstem response (ABR) latencies increased and amplitudes decreased with increasing stimulus repetition rate for human newborns and adults.

Title: Basic characteristics of click-evoked otoacoustic emissions in infants and children.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants, toddlers, children, and young adults
Outcome: click-evoked otoacoustic emissions (COAEs); spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs)
Evidence_Quote: The purpose of the current study was to determine basic characteristics of COAEs in infants, toddlers, children, and young adults

Title: Basic characteristics of distortion product otoacoustic emissions in infants and children.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants, toddlers, children, and young adults
Outcome: distortion product otoacoustic emissions (DPOAEs); spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs)
Evidence_Quote: DPOAE input/output (I/O) functions at seven f2 frequencies and SOAEs were measured from one ear of 196 subjects.

Title: Organization and discrimination of repeating sound sequences by newborn infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: discrimination of repeated rising and falling four-tone sequences; auditory stream organization
Evidence_Quote: A series of three experiments investigated the ability of 3- to 4-day-old infants to discriminate repeated rising and falling four-tone sequences in two configurations of source timbre and spatial position.

Title: Effects of three parameters on speaking fundamental frequency.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: speaking fundamental frequency
Evidence_Quote: it was observed that, in general, oral reading resulted in higher mean SFF's than those for spontaneous speech.

Title: Features of the auditory development of the short-tailed Brazilian opossum, Monodelphis domestica: evoked responses, neonatal vocalizations and synapses in the inferior colliculus.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: short-tailed Brazilian opossum (Monodelphis domestica) pups, postnatal days 24-40
Stimulus_Type: click stimuli (evoked potentials); pup isolation calls
Outcome: hearing onset at postnatal day 24 with threshold 83 dB SPL, declining below 58 dB by day 40; isolation call peaks near 13 kHz
Evidence_Quote: Evoked potentials were first recorded at postnatal day 24 at a threshold of 83 dB SPL; thresholds declined over subsequent weeks to below 58 dB at 40 days. Isolation calls emitted by the pups had stereotypic spectra with peaks at near 13 kHz and an octave higher.

Title: Cochlear pathology induced by aminoglycoside ototoxicity during postnatal maturation in cats.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: hair cell degeneration progresses from base to apex; spiral ganglion loss in the middle cochlea (approximately 2.8-8 kHz) is independent of hair cell loss
Evidence_Quote: with initial cell loss occurring in the middle of the cochlea, about 40-60% from the base (approximately 2.8-8 kHz)

Title: Infants' pitch perception: masking by low- and high-frequency noises.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: pure tones and harmonic tonal complexes (missing fundamental), presented with low- or high-frequency noise
Outcome: infants discriminate pure tones in high-frequency noise but not low-frequency noise, and categorize missing-fundamental complexes like adults, indicating central pitch processing
Evidence_Quote: Adults and infants were presented with either pure tones of 160 and 200 Hz or harmonic tonal complexes with pitches equivalent to 160 and 200 Hz.

Title: Perceptual differences in infant cries revealed by modifications of acoustic features.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: perceptual ratings
Evidence_Quote: In a perceptual rating task, higher-F0 cries as well as cries with larger amounts of jitter tended to be given more negative ratings than were lower-F0 cries and cries with less jitter, respectively.

Title: Do weak syllables count for newborns?
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: discrimination of weak-strong words from strong words
Evidence_Quote: Two-day-old French infants were tested on their capacity to discriminate phonetically highly varied words containing syllables with various strong vowels versus the weak, reduced vowel schwa in natural, isolated English words.

Title: Adult and infant perception of two English phones.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: discrimination
Evidence_Quote: English listeners of three ages (6-8 months, 10-12 months, and adults) were presented with the phonetic difference, [da] vs [t = a].
